title: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Ziruz, Son of Rabbi Meir’s Father-in-Law
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Zeiruz, son of the father-in-law of Rabbi Meir.

He was Rabbi Meir’s student, as in Chullin 6b. Jerusalem Talmud Demai 2:1 relates that he testified before Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi that Rabbi Meir ate a vegetable leaf in Beit Shean; on that basis Rabbi permitted Beit Shean. In Shabbat 146a,
he tells Rabbi, “Rabbi Meir did not hold a person liable for a sin offering in such a case.”

notes.text: The words ובשבת קמו. are the citation Shabbat 146a, not a claim that people arose on Shabbat. Rabbi Meir is the authority ruling on liability, not the person supposedly liable for the offering. Son of Meir’s father-in-law describes a brother-in-law relationship.

Chullin 6b directly names Yehoshua ben Zeruz and the vegetable-leaf testimony. The supplied Shabbat 146a locator and closing sin-offering clause are retained from Hyman; the bounded consulted Shabbat passages did not independently establish that clause.
